issues.legal_issue: A legislature may retrospectively validate conduct affected by a prior judgment by changing the legal basis on which the judgment rested, rather than merely declaring the judgment ineffective.
material_facts: An earlier judgment held construction on acquired land unlawful because the agreement governing the acquisition prohibited construction there.
The legislature amended the governing law retrospectively to remove that prohibition and validate specified development and construction carried out under statutory permissions.
The relevant legislative field included acquisition and requisition of property.
issues.conclusion: The legislature was competent to enact the amendment retrospectively because it removed the basis of the earlier judgment; the amendment did not merely overrule that judgment.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature with competence over the subject may enact retrospective validating legislation if it removes the defect or legal basis on which a court decision rested and remains consistent with constitutional limitations. It cannot simply declare a judicial decision nonbinding. Bhaktwar Trust v. M.D. Narayan states the test of legislative competence, removal of the defect, and consistency with Part III. Madan Mohan Pathak v. Union of India cautions against retrospectively depriving accrued rights arising from a judgment. The Court also relied on Entry 42 of List III of the Seventh Schedule.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_validating_l: A party brings a constitutional challenge to legislation intended to validate conduct affected by a prior judicial decision.
predicates.legislature_acts_within_assigned_field: The legislature enacts the measure in a subject area assigned to it.
predicates.amendment_removes_basis_of_prior_judgmen: The legislature changes the underlying legal rule on which the prior judgment depended.
predicates.amendment_does_not_merely_nullify_judgme: The legislation changes the governing law rather than only declaring that the prior judgment has no effect.

issues.definition: When a legislature acts within its assigned field and changes the legal basis of a prior judgment rather than merely nullifying it, a retrospective validation measure may be upheld.

issues.legal_issue: A state amendment is not repugnant to central legislation when the two can operate together and the central legislation does not prohibit the change made by the amendment.
material_facts: The central legislation and the agreement made under it did not provide for modification, variation, or deletion of the agreement’s terms.
The state amendment provided for retrospective modification of such agreements and removed the prohibition on construction in the agreement.
The amendment did not create a direct, irreconcilable conflict with the central legislation.
issues.conclusion: The state amendment was not repugnant to the central legislation, so the challenge based on Article 254 failed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 254, repugnancy requires clear and direct inconsistency that is irreconcilable and makes it impossible to obey both laws. The Court relied on M. Karunanidhi v. Union of India and Kanaka Gruha Nirmana Sahakara Sangha v. Narayanamma. It considered Sections 41 and 42 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, and held that the central legislation was silent on modification of the agreement, so the state amendment did not place the laws in direct conflict.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_state_amendm: A party challenges a state legislative measure on the ground that it conflicts with central legislation.
predicates.central_law_is_silent_on_agreement_modif: The central legislation does not address whether the relevant agreement may be changed or its terms deleted.
predicates.state_amendment_adds_modification_mechan: The state legislature enacts a measure providing for changes to agreements made under the central law.
predicates.both_laws_can_operate_together: The central law and the state measure do not impose commands that cannot both be followed.

issues.definition: A state amendment is not repugnant when it adds a mechanism on a subject left unaddressed by central law and the two measures can operate together.

issues.legal_issue: Legislative provisions preventing enforcement of judicial orders concerning conduct validated by an amendment do not unlawfully displace judicial power when they are incidental and consequential to a valid change in the underlying law.
material_facts: The amendment changed the legal basis for the earlier judicial determination by removing the agreement’s prohibition on construction and validating specified conduct.
The amendment also restricted proceedings seeking cancellation or demolition of construction validated under the amended law.
The Court treated those restrictions concerning court orders as incidental and consequential to the validation measure.
issues.conclusion: The challenge based on the rule of law and judicial review did not succeed because the provisions concerning court orders were incidental and consequential to the validating amendment.
issues.legal_principle: A legislature cannot simply set aside a court’s decision, but it may change the underlying law and enact provisions consequential to validating conduct under that changed law. The Court applied the validation principles discussed in Bhaktwar Trust v. M.D. Narayan.

predicates.challenge_alleges_interference_with_judi: A party argues that legislation concerning the effect or enforcement of judicial orders interferes with judicial power.
predicates.amendment_changes_underlying_legal_basis: The legislature changes the legal rule on which the prior judicial determination depended.
predicates.order_related_bar_is_incidental_to_valid: The restriction on proceedings or enforcement operates as a consequence of validating conduct under the changed legal rule.

issues.definition: When an amendment changes the underlying legal rule and a restriction concerning judicial orders is consequential to that change, the restriction does not unlawfully displace judicial power.
